findings.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParseReturnType object ({success, data}), but the Google caller stores that whole wrapper as the credential key, whereas the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse() call stored the parsed credential object itself. After the first token refresh, prisma.credential.update persists {success: true, data: {...}} into credential.key instead of the credential object; every subsequent consumer that reads credential.key.access_token / credential.key.expiry_date gets undefined, so Google Calendar integration breaks for all users after any refresh, regardless of whether credential sharing is enabled.

[BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] evaluate to single literal keys (ZodType has no toString override, so the key is the literal string "[object Object]"), not catchall patterns, so the 'any property with a number is the expiry' assumption does not work and zod's default unknown-key stripping drops expiry_date and every other field except access_token. When credential sharing is enabled, every parsed refresh response yields data = {access_token} only (plus refresh_token overwritten with the literal placeholder "refresh_token"), so the expiry date is silently lost from stored credentials and expiry-based re-auth logic reads undefined.

[BUG] In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but the Google caller immediately does res?.data and then token.access_token, treating it as a gaxios response whose .data is the parsed token body. With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, a Google Calendar token refresh crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading access_token)' because a fetch Response has no .data property, breaking calendar reads/writes for every user with a Google credential.

[BUG] In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but the Zoho Bigin caller immediately evaluates tokenInfo.data.error, which only exists on an axios response object. With credential sharing enabled, a Zoho Bigin token refresh throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading error)' because Response.data is undefined, crashing the Bigin calendar service instead of refreshing tokens.

[BUG] In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but the ZohoCRM caller immediately evaluates zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error, which only exists on an axios response object. With credential sharing enabled, a ZohoCRM token refresh throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading error)' because a fetch Response has no .data property, crashing the ZohoCRM calendar service.

[BUG] In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but the Hubspot caller types and uses the result as HubspotToken (a parsed token object with accessToken/expiresIn), so downstream property reads get undefined. With credential sharing enabled, expiry is computed from hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn === undefined, producing NaN/expired expiry dates and tokens read as undefined, corrupting the stored Hubspot credential and failing all subsequent Hubspot API calls.

[BUG] The rename of _utils/createOAuthAppCredential.ts, decodeOAuthState.ts and encodeOAuthState.ts into _utils/oauth/ is not accompanied by updates to all importers in the diff — at minimum packages/app-store/closecom/api/add.ts and callback.ts still import the old paths ../../_utils/createOAuthAppCredential and ../../_utils/decodeOAuthState, which no longer exist. TypeScript/Next build fails with 'Module not found' for the not-updated app-store packages, so the branch does not compile until every remaining importer is migrated.

[ADVISORY] A new unconditional network call to login.salesforce.com plus a prisma.credential.update is inserted immediately before jsforce.Connection creation, which runs on every SalesforceCalendarService construction, where previously the connection reused stored tokens and jsforce refreshed only on demand. Every operation that instantiates the service (event bookings, availability checks, cron availability scans) now pays a blocking Salesforce token round-trip and a DB write even when the stored access_token is still valid; a Salesforce outage or added latency directly slows booking flows that previously never hit Salesforce at construction time.

[ADVISORY] The function overwrites a missing refresh_token with the literal placeholder string 'refresh_token', and callers persist this placeholder into credential.key in place of the real refresh token. A self-hoster who enables credential sharing (sync mode supplies only access tokens) and later disables it is left with credentials whose refresh_token is the literal string 'refresh_token', so reverting to normal OAuth refresh fails for every affected user until they manually re-authorize each app.

[ADVISORY] The setup comment states CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY 'must be 32 bytes for AES256 encryption algorithm' but then instructs generating it with `openssl rand -base64 24`, which yields 24 bytes (32 base64 characters). Self-hosters following the comment will generate a key that contradicts the stated 32-byte requirement and then mismatch the parent application if the parent generated a 32-byte key, producing undecryptable credentials on the webhook endpoint with no error pointing at the key mismatch.

[BUG] In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response, and the Google refresh code then executes `const token = res?.data;` followed by `googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token`, which throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'access_token'). Every token refresh for google-calendar crashes with a 500 whenever APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set — calendar reads/writes for all Google credentials fail until the feature is disabled.

[BUG] In sync mode `hubspotRefreshToken` is an unawaited fetch Response object, but the unchanged downstream code reads `hubspotRefreshToken.access_token` and `hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token` and persists the result, writing undefined tokens into the credential key. First Hubspot token refresh under credential sync replaces a working credential with access_token: undefined — Hubspot calendar sync breaks for every synced user and the corrupted key is persisted via prisma.credential.update.

[BUG] In sync mode `tokenInfo` is a raw fetch Response (not an axios result), so the unchanged check `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)` throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error'). Zoho Bigin token refresh crashes with a 500 on every invocation when credential sync is enabled, taking down Bigin calendar operations for all synced users.

[BUG] In sync mode `zohoCrmTokenInfo` is a raw fetch Response instead of an axios response, so the unchanged `if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error)` throws TypeError on undefined `.data`. Zoho CRM token refresh crashes with an unhandled error on every refresh when credential sync is enabled, breaking Zoho CRM calendar sync for all synced users.

[BUG] The zoho-bigin call passes `credentialId` (the credential row's id, per the class's existing `this.credentialId = credential.id` wiring) where refreshOAuthTokens' contract and every other call site pass `credential.userId`, so the sync request sends calcomUserId=<credential.id>. The sync endpoint is queried with the wrong identifier: the parent cal.com looks up a non-existent user (404 / failed refresh) or — if ids collide with a real user — returns and persists another user's credentials into this credential row.

[BUG] Salesforce is the only refreshed app not routed through refreshOAuthTokens: it performs a hardcoded direct fetch using `credentialKey.refresh_token`, which in sync mode is either absent or the literal placeholder string "refresh_token" written by parseRefreshTokenResponse. With credential sync enabled, every Salesforce refresh sends refresh_token="refresh_token" to login.salesforce.com, fails, and throws — Salesforce calendar sync is completely broken under the exact configuration this PR introduces.

[BUG] When the parsed response lacks refresh_token (always true for the sync endpoint, whose documented response contains only access_token and expiry), the function mutates data to `refresh_token: "refresh_token"`, and callers (googlecalendar CalendarService.ts ~98-101, office365calendar CalendarService.ts ~263-270) then persist this merged/stripped object over the credential key via prisma.credential.update. Sync-mode refreshes overwrite the stored credential with a placeholder refresh_token and drop expiry_date and other real fields; if CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is ever removed or the sync endpoint is down, previously-working Google and Outlook credentials are permanently broken (no valid refresh_token to fall back to).

[BUG] The computed schema keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` each evaluate to a single constant string, so the intended "any property with a number is the expiry" wildcard never exists — the schema degenerates to effectively `{ access_token: string }` and the expiry date the sync contract promises ("The response should only contain the access token and expiry date") is silently discarded. Expiry returned by the sync endpoint is never parsed or persisted, so consumers that rely on expiry_date (e.g. Google's isExpired pre-check) see credentials as perpetually expired and hit the sync endpoint on every request instead of only near expiry.

[BUG] The webhook handler has no error handling around `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)`, `symmetricDecrypt(...)`, or `JSON.parse(...)` — a malformed body, wrong encryption key, or invalid ciphertext throws an unhandled ZodError/crypto error and the route returns a 500. Any misconfigured or malformed sync push from the parent cal.com gets a 500 instead of a 4xx, and operators get no diagnostic signal distinguishing a bad key from a bad payload; retries from the parent will keep failing identically.

[ADVISORY] The diff introduces three non-trivial new behaviors — the credential-injection webhook endpoint (header auth, AES decryption, credential upsert), refreshOAuthTokens' sync-mode dispatch, and parseRefreshTokenResponse's dual-schema normalization — and contains zero test files (scanned the diff for spec/**, test/**, *.spec.*, *.test.*: none present), so none of the sync-mode paths that this review shows crashing or corrupting credentials are caught by CI. The exact failure modes above (Response-object misuse, placeholder refresh_token persistence, wrong userId for zoho-bigin) ship to production unverified; any regression in the webhook's auth or decryption also lands silently since no assertion covers this route.

[ADVISORY] The webhook endpoint gates only on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED (i.e. CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET + CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY) while every consumer of the sync feature (refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse) additionally requires CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, leaving the two gates of the same feature out of sync. A self-hosted operator who sets the webhook secret and encryption key but no sync endpoint gets a live, writable credential-injection webhook while their own instance never participates in token refresh — credentials injected by the parent will sit and rot as tokens expire with no local refresh path, and the half-enabled state is invisible in .env.example's setup instructions.

[ADVISORY] The newly added Salesforce refresh block runs unconditionally inside connection setup — every time a jsforce.Connection is constructed the code fetches a fresh token from login.salesforce.com and writes it via prisma.credential.update, regardless of whether the existing access_token is expired. On any deployment with salesforce installed, each calendar operation that builds a service adds one outbound token request plus one credential DB write to the hot path, multiplying Salesforce API consumption and credential-row churn; token endpoint rate limits now gate ordinary calendar reads.

[BUG] In sync mode the fetch Response returned by refreshOAuthTokens is passed directly to handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>, which expects Lark's envelope ({ code, data: { access_token, expire_time, ... } }), while the sync endpoint's documented response is a bare minimal token payload. With credential sync enabled, Lark token refresh cannot extract an access token from the sync response (the Lark envelope fields are absent), so Lark calendar operations fail on every refresh — lark is wired into the sync dispatch but not adapted to the minimal response shape it will receive.

[BUG] refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response in sync mode while callers destructure app-specific shapes ({res}, .data, HubspotToken fields), so the credential-sync happy path throws or reads undefined for Google, Hubspot, Zoho and Zoho-Bigin. With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set (the feature's advertised deployment), googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts executes `const token = res?.data` on a fetch Response, gets undefined, then throws a TypeError on `token.access_token`; hubspot, zohocrm (`zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`) and zoho-bigin (`tokenInfo.data.error`) likewise dereference .data/fields that a Response does not have, so every token refresh in sharing mode crashes the calendar call instead of syncing credentials. The sync endpoint response contract was never adapted per app — the feature's core path was not traced through its own call sites.

[BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema uses `z.string().toString()` as computed keys, which evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" for both entries (the second overwrites the first), so the schema enforces nothing and zod's default strip mode drops access_token and expiry fields from the parsed data. In sync mode, parseRefreshTokenResponse returns data with access_token/expiry stripped: Google persists a credential key missing access_token and expiry_date via prisma.credential.update, so subsequent Google Calendar API calls fail authentication; the Salesforce caller spreads accessTokenParsed.data and loses instance_url, breaking the jsforce connection. The comment's stated invariant ("any property with a number is the expiry") is not enforced by any schema logic — the validation is a no-op that also corrupts stored credentials.

[BUG] The new Salesforce refresh block never routes through refreshOAuthTokens, so when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set it still refreshes against login.salesforce.com using this instance's own client_id/client_secret. For the stated audience (self-hosters whose parent application holds the real Salesforce app credentials), the local instance's client_secret does not match the parent's OAuth app, so the refresh call fails with invalid_client and Salesforce calendar sync is broken in exactly the deployments the feature targets — the sync feature is inconsistently scoped across the apps it touches in this diff.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse overwrites a missing refresh_token with the literal string "refresh_token" unconditionally — including in non-sync mode where the real provider refresh flow is used — and the fabricated value is then persisted to prisma.credential. A deployment that later disables credential sharing is left with credentials whose stored refresh_token is the placeholder "refresh_token"; the next real provider refresh sends that placeholder and the provider rejects it, permanently breaking that integration's token renewal with corrupted data written by the app itself.

[ADVISORY] The redirectUri is changed from the appConfig.slug interpolation to a hardcoded `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback`, a drive-by change unrelated to credential sync. Behavior is unchanged only while appConfig.slug happens to be "zoho-bigin"; the slug now has two sources of truth (config.json for the callback handler, hardcoded string here), and the appConfig import in this file becomes dead for the URL — the next slug or rename change silently desyncs the add/callback pair. Not traceable to any requirement in this PR.

[ADVISORY] The new refresh fetch runs unconditionally before every jsforce connection creation (not gated on token expiry), and its success check `response.statusText !== "OK"` breaks under HTTP/2 where statusText is an empty string. Every Salesforce calendar operation now pays an extra token-refresh HTTP round trip plus a prisma.credential.update even when the stored token is still valid (hot-path regression on a path previously served with zero extra calls), and on any HTTP/2 response the statusText check throws HttpError 400 even for a successful refresh, disabling Salesforce sync entirely on such connections.

[ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is exported as the result of `&&` on two env strings (type string | undefined, not boolean), unlike every other boolean flag pattern in this constants file. Every consumer (webhook handler, parseRefreshTokenResponse, refreshOAuthTokens) must remember it is a truthy string rather than a boolean; the next consumer that does a strict `=== true` check or type-narrows it silently mis-gates the feature, and the exported surface documents the wrong contract for the flag.

[ADVISORY] The entire credential-sync feature surface added in this diff (webhook handler, refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse, and the per-app refresh rewiring across 7 services) ships with zero tests. The findings above (Response-shape mismatch, stripped schema keys, placeholder refresh_token) are exactly the class of regression tests would have caught; any future change to the sync contract or to one of the seven rewired refreshAccessToken closures silently breaks calendar/video syncing for all users of that app, discovered only at booking time.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper ({success, data}), and the Google refresh path persists that wrapper object directly as the credential key (`data: { key }`), replacing the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` which returned the bare credentials. After the first token refresh, credential.key in the DB is `{success:true, data:{access_token,...}}` instead of the credentials object; every later GoogleCalendarService read (`credential.key as GoogleCredentials`) sees undefined access_token/refresh_token at the top level, so Google Calendar auth breaks for that user until manual repair.

[BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but its callers destructure provider-specific shapes: Google does `res?.data` (googleauth result shape) and Hubspot/Zoho-Bigin treat the return value as a parsed token/axios response. With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED + CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, Google's `token.access_token` throws TypeError (Response has no `.data`), and Hubspot/Zoho-Bigin read undefined token fields and persist undefined/NaN expiry into credential rows — token refresh is broken and can destroy stored credentials for every sync-mode deployment.

[BUG] The minimumTokenResponseSchema catch-all keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the string "[object Object]" (Object.prototype.toString on a Zod instance), so the schema is `{access_token, "[object Object]"}` and the intended 'any numeric property is the expiry' wildcard never matches; zod's default stripping then drops every field except access_token. In sync mode the parsed token response contains only access_token — expiry_date/expires_in and any other fields are silently stripped, so downstream expiry computations get undefined/NaN even once the Response-shape bug is fixed.

[BUG] The Zoho-Bigin refresh call passes `credentialId` as the userId argument of refreshOAuthTokens, while every other call site (google-calendar, hubspot, zohocrm, lark, zoom, webex, o365) passes `credential.userId` — a confusable-pair binding where the credential row id is sent as calcomUserId. In sync mode the CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT receives the credential's database id in the `calcomUserId` field, so the parent application resolves the wrong user (or none) and returns/updates credentials for the wrong account, silently corrupting or failing Zoho-Bigin token sync.

[BUG] Salesforce is the only app whose refresh path was not routed through refreshOAuthTokens — it performs a direct hardcoded fetch to login.salesforce.com unconditionally, creating a parallel refresh service path outside the credential-sync architecture introduced in this diff. In a credential-sharing deployment, Salesforce refreshes tokens directly against the provider (rotating the refresh token), so cal.com's stored copy diverges and is invalidated — the shared-credential invariant this PR establishes is broken for the salesforce app.

[BUG] The webhook uses findFirst-then-update/create (explicitly noted 'Can't use prisma upsert') with no unique constraint on Credential(userId, appId) backing the check, so concurrent webhook deliveries race the SELECT and both fall into the create branch. Two concurrent sync pushes for the same user+app create duplicate Credential rows; downstream code that picks the user's calendar/video credential gets an ambiguous, possibly stale duplicate, and every subsequent webhook updates only one of the rows while reads may select the other.

[ADVISORY] The newly added Salesforce token-refresh fetch and prisma.credential.update run unconditionally on every service construction, with no expiry check, on a hot path (every calendar operation instantiates the service). Every Salesforce calendar read/write now issues an external token HTTP call plus a DB write even when the stored token is still valid, adding latency and provider rate-limit pressure to the booking path for all Salesforce users.

[ADVISORY] The sync-mode fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout, no response.ok/status check, and no retry or fallback, and it sits synchronously inside token refresh on the booking path. A slow or erroring credential-sync endpoint hangs or degrades every calendar/video operation for all users (fetch has no default timeout), turning one dependent service into a global availability dependency with no graceful degradation.

[ADVISORY] The decrypted `keys` payload is JSON.parse'd and persisted via credential.create/update with no per-app zod schema validation, unlike every other credential write path in the app-store which validates before persisting. A payload encrypted with a wrong/mismatched key decrypts to garbage or a wrong-shaped object that is stored verbatim as the user's credential key, silently bricking that user's app integration with no validation error to surface the cause.

[ADVISORY] When the token response has no refresh_token, the code writes the literal sentinel string "refresh_token" into the parsed data, which callers then persist as the credential's real refresh_token. The sentinel is stored as data in the DB; if CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is later unset while APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED stays on (or vice versa), the next direct refresh sends the literal string "refresh_token" to the provider as a refresh token, permanently breaking that credential's refresh.

[ADVISORY] Credential matching is keyed on (userId, appId) only, but Credential rows created before appId existed (or by paths that set only `type`) have appId null, so the lookup misses them and the create branch inserts a second credential with the same `type` for the same user. Legacy installs accumulate duplicate credentials per app per user; consumers that pick the user's calendar credential by type now face multiple rows with no defined winner, so bookings may bind to the stale non-synced copy.

[ADVISORY] The design establishes two concurrent writers for the same credential records — a push webhook (app-credential.ts) and a pull refresh endpoint (refreshOAuthTokens) — with no coordination, versioning, or single-source-of-truth rule for which copy wins. When parent and child both refresh (e.g. a scheduled refresh on cal.com racing a booking-triggered refresh on the child), each side persists its own newer token and last-writer-wins; for providers that rotate refresh tokens the losing side's stored refresh_token is invalidated, permanently breaking that user's integration.

[BUG] When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but the following line reads res?.data, which is undefined on a Response, so token.access_token throws TypeError. Every Google Calendar token refresh for a self-hoster with credential sync enabled crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading access_token)' instead of refreshing the token, breaking the exact workflow this PR ships.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the SafeParseReturn wrapper object ({success, data}), and this call site stores that wrapper directly as credential.key, whereas the replaced code stored googleCredentialSchema.parse(...) output (the parsed data itself). For ALL deployments including those with credential sharing disabled, after the first successful token refresh credential.key becomes {success:true, data:{...}}; the next refresh reads access_token off the wrapper, gets undefined, and Google Calendar integration is permanently broken until the user reinstalls the app.

[BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, and the immediately following retained code evaluates tokenInfo.data.error — Response has no .data property, so tokenInfo.data is undefined and .error throws TypeError. With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, every Zoho Bigin token refresh crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading error)' instead of refreshing credentials.

[BUG] Same contract mismatch as zoho-bigin: in sync mode zohoCrmTokenInfo is a fetch Response, and the retained code reads zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error, throwing TypeError because .data is undefined on a Response. With credential sync enabled, every Zoho CRM token refresh crashes instead of refreshing the credential.

[BUG] The refreshed value is annotated and consumed as HubspotToken (an object with accessToken etc. from hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken), but in sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, which is then used downstream as if it were the parsed token. With credential sync enabled, HubSpot's credential update writes a serialized Response object (or undefined token fields) into credential.key, corrupting the HubSpot integration the next time it is used.

[BUG] The computed schema keys z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString() evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", so the second (optional) key silently overwrites the first and minimumTokenResponseSchema is effectively {access_token: string} — it neither validates the intended numeric expiry field nor retains any extra field. In sync mode every refreshed token response is stripped down to access_token alone: expiry data from the sync endpoint is discarded (callers fall back to stale expiry, causing repeated spurious refreshes), and any contract the sync endpoint was supposed to honor is not actually enforced.

[BUG] The refresh_token placeholder injection (data.refresh_token = "refresh_token") runs unconditionally — including in the non-sync path where the caller passes the real provider schema — and office365calendar's refreshAccessToken spreads tokenResponse.data over the existing credentials, so a response lacking refresh_token overwrites the stored real refresh token with the literal string "refresh_token". For a deployment without credential sync, one refresh cycle in which Microsoft omits refresh_token permanently replaces the user's real refresh token with a placeholder in the database; all subsequent refreshes fail and the user must reinstall the app.

[ADVISORY] The iteration silently changed failure semantics for the pre-existing path: the console.error zodError logging was removed and the code now throws via parseRefreshTokenResponse on schema failure, ungated by APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED. Existing self-hosters who never enable credential sync lose the previous graceful behavior (log and continue with stale-but-usable credentials) and instead get a thrown error on any malformed Microsoft token response — an objective change smuggled into the sync PR without being called out for acceptance.

[ADVISORY] This block adds an unconditional Salesforce token refresh (remote POST + credential DB write) on the connection-creation path that previously served directly from cached credentialKey, plus a hardcoded login.salesforce.com URL and a dead `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` check (parseRefreshTokenResponse already throws on failure). Every Salesforce calendar operation pays an extra token-endpoint round-trip and a DB write per connection creation, a hot-path regression unrelated to the stated credential-sync objective that entered the PR without its own acceptance; the hardcoded URL also ignores instance_url for custom Salesforce domains.

[ADVISORY] The redirect URI was silently changed from the config-driven `/api/integrations/${appConfig.slug}/callback` to a hardcoded "/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback", an unexplained objective change unrelated to credential sync. The next contributor who changes appConfig.slug (or copies this pattern to another app) now has two places to update; if slug and the hardcoded string ever diverge the OAuth redirect URI breaks against the provider-registered value.

[ADVISORY] The webhook secret is compared with a plain !== string comparison rather than a timing-safe comparison. A self-hoster enabling credential sync exposes CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET to a remote timing side channel over this unauthenticated endpoint; an attacker who recovers it can push arbitrary credentials into any user's account.

[ADVISORY] The decrypted keys are JSON.parse'd and stored directly as credential.key with no validation against the app's credential schema, and JSON.parse/symmetricDecrypt failures propagate as unhandled 500s. A malformed or wrong-shape payload from the parent instance poisons the user's credential silently (the webhook returns 200), and the integration then fails at usage time with schema/crash errors that are far from the actual cause; any thrown ZodError/JSON parse error also surfaces as a 500 instead of the 4xx the contract implies.

[ADVISORY] appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse throws ZodError on a malformed body, which Next converts to a 500 rather than a 400. Callers sending a bad payload (or an attacker probing the endpoint) receive a 500 server error, polluting error monitoring and misrepresenting client-side input errors as server faults.

[ADVISORY] The findFirst-then-update/create sequence is not atomic, and the inline comment acknowledges upsert was rejected — two concurrent webhooks for the same userId+appId both observe no credential and both create one. Concurrent credential-sync deliveries for the same user produce duplicate Credential rows for the same app, after which findFirst picks an arbitrary one for updates and the stale duplicate keeps being used or refreshed inconsistently.

[ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is declared as a constant but its value is the string|undefined result of an && of two env vars (not a boolean), and the enablement condition `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is hand-duplicated in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts and refreshOAuthTokens.ts. TypeScript will not flag boolean misuse of the constant, and the next change to the gating (e.g., adding a third env var) applied to only one of the two duplicated sites leaves token fetching and token parsing half-enabled, producing refreshes from the sync endpoint parsed with the wrong schema.

[BUG] The webhook secret is verified with a plain `!==` string comparison (`req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`), which is not constant-time, and the endpoint has no rate limiting on the secret check. An attacker who can reach this endpoint can mount a timing side-channel (assisted by unthrottled retry) against the shared secret; each recovered secret grants the ability to inject/overwrite OAuth credentials for ANY userId, i.e. takeover of arbitrary users' calendar/CRM integrations. The correct control is a constant-time comparison (e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual) plus rate limiting, neither of which exists in this diff.

[ADVISORY] Authentication for a credential-injection endpoint that can write keys for any userId rests on a single static, non-rotatable shared header value, with no HMAC signature, timestamp, or nonce, so valid requests are replayable by design and one leaked secret compromises every user at once. Whoever captures one legitimate webhook request (proxy logs, the plaintext custom header on a non-TLS self-hosted deployment) can replay it indefinitely, and any operator of any child instance holding the shared secret can write credentials into any other instance/user reachable with the same secret. There is no per-request binding, no replay window, and no way to rotate without coordinating every deployment.

[ADVISORY] The decrypted credential payload is `JSON.parse`d and written directly to `credential.key` with no schema validation at this trust boundary. Anything the sender produces (a misconfigured encryption key, a buggy sync sender, or a holder of the webhook secret) is persisted verbatim as the app's credential; the malformed shape surfaces only later, inside booking/calendar flows that consume `credential.key`, causing hard-to-trace runtime failures far from the write that caused them.

[ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is implicitly truthy whenever both `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` are set, with no explicit opt-in flag. An operator who sets CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET for any other webhook purpose silently activates the new public credential-injection endpoint and switches all OAuth token refreshes to the sync endpoint — a security-posture and behavior change triggered by environment presence rather than a deliberate feature flag that can be turned off without a code change.

[ADVISORY] When sharing is enabled, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` strips every field except `access_token` (the computed `[z.string().toString()]` keys collapse to a single literal non-matching key), so `data.refresh_token` is always undefined and the code overwrites the credential's real refresh token with the literal string `"refresh_token"`, which callers then persist via `prisma.credential.update`. The first token refresh under sharing mode irreversibly replaces stored refresh tokens with the placeholder for providers whose refresh path goes through parse (office365, zoom, webex, lark, zoho). adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when sync mode is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), the function executes `fetch(...)` and returns the raw `Response` object (not `await response.json()` / parsed token data). In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` assigns `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and downstream logic (not changed in the diff) will treat it like a token object. Under sync mode it will instead be a `Response`, so properties like `access_token` / `refresh_token` will be `undefined`, leading to broken refresh behavior and likely persisting bad credential data if the existing code updates prisma with those fields. The finding’s “unawaited” wording is slightly off (the fetch is awaited), but the core defect (returning a `Response` where token data is expected) is directly shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sync mode `tokenInfo` is a raw fetch Response (not an axios result), so the unchanged check `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)` throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error'). Zoho Bigin token refresh crashes with a 500 on every invocation when credential sync is enabled, taking down Bigin calendar operations for all synced users.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, the helper returns a raw `fetch(...)` Response. In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `tokenInfo` is obtained via `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` but the subsequent unchanged logic still treats it like an axios result: `if (!tokenInfo.data.error) { ... }`. A `Response` object has no `.data`, so `tokenInfo.data` is `undefined` and accessing `.error` will throw a `TypeError`, causing token refresh to fail (500) in sync mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sync mode `zohoCrmTokenInfo` is a raw fetch Response instead of an axios response, so the unchanged `if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error)` throws TypeError on undefined `.data`. Zoho CRM token refresh crashes with an unhandled error on every refresh when credential sync is enabled, breaking Zoho CRM calendar sync for all synced users.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the token refresh call is now wrapped with `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and the result is still treated like an axios response (`if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error) { ... }`). But `refreshOAuthTokens` (new in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) returns a raw `fetch` `Response` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy. A `fetch` Response does not have a `.data` property, so in sync mode `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` is `undefined` and accessing `.error` will throw, breaking refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The zoho-bigin call passes `credentialId` (the credential row's id, per the class's existing `this.credentialId = credential.id` wiring) where refreshOAuthTokens' contract and every other call site pass `credential.userId`, so the sync request sends calcomUserId=<credential.id>. The sync endpoint is queried with the wrong identifier: the parent cal.com looks up a non-existent user (404 / failed refresh) or — if ids collide with a real user — returns and persists another user's credentials into this credential row.
matched_golden_ids: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: a call to `refreshOAuthTokens` incorrectly passes `credentialId` instead of `credential.userId`, causing the sync endpoint/user lookup to use the wrong identifier, leading to failed refreshes or even syncing the wrong user’s credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Salesforce is the only refreshed app not routed through refreshOAuthTokens: it performs a hardcoded direct fetch using `credentialKey.refresh_token`, which in sync mode is either absent or the literal placeholder string "refresh_token" written by parseRefreshTokenResponse. With credential sync enabled, every Salesforce refresh sends refresh_token="refresh_token" to login.salesforce.com, fails, and throws — Salesforce calendar sync is completely broken under the exact configuration this PR introduces.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, token refresh is implemented via a direct `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` using `credentialKey.refresh_token` and is not routed through the new `refreshOAuthTokens` abstraction that other OAuth apps were updated to use. Under the PR’s new “credential sync” mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` + `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), the shared refresh flow is designed to work even when `refresh_token` is missing by using `parseRefreshTokenResponse` to tolerate minimal responses and even writing a placeholder `refresh_token` string when absent. Because Salesforce bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, it will still attempt to refresh against Salesforce using whatever is stored in `credential.key.refresh_token` (which, in sync mode, can be missing or become the placeholder), causing refresh to fail and the code to throw (`if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw ...`). This breaks Salesforce refresh behavior under the configuration this PR introduces.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When the parsed response lacks refresh_token (always true for the sync endpoint, whose documented response contains only access_token and expiry), the function mutates data to `refresh_token: "refresh_token"`, and callers (googlecalendar CalendarService.ts ~98-101, office365calendar CalendarService.ts ~263-270) then persist this merged/stripped object over the credential key via prisma.credential.update. Sync-mode refreshes overwrite the stored credential with a placeholder refresh_token and drop expiry_date and other real fields; if CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is ever removed or the sync endpoint is down, previously-working Google and Outlook credentials are permanently broken (no valid refresh_token to fall back to).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when sync-mode is enabled it accepts responses without `refresh_token` and then forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the result is merged into the existing credential via `{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`, which will overwrite a previously valid `refresh_token` with the placeholder when the sync endpoint returns only `access_token`/expiry. That can permanently corrupt stored credentials and break future non-sync refreshes. (The finding’s mention of Google Calendar specifically overwriting due to the placeholder is less directly supported because Google passes `googleCredentials`—which already contains a refresh_token—into `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, but the Office365 overwrite scenario is clearly shown.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The computed schema keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` each evaluate to a single constant string, so the intended "any property with a number is the expiry" wildcard never exists — the schema degenerates to effectively `{ access_token: string }` and the expiry date the sync contract promises ("The response should only contain the access token and expiry date") is silently discarded. Expiry returned by the sync endpoint is never parsed or persisted, so consumers that rely on expiry_date (e.g. Google's isExpired pre-check) see credentials as perpetually expired and hit the sync endpoint on every request instead of only near expiry.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. In JS/TS this evaluates to a single constant property name (e.g. "ZodString"/"[object Object]"), not a wildcard/index signature. As a result the schema does not model “any numeric property is expiry”; instead it either (a) requires a nonsense constant key and will fail `safeParse` for normal token responses, causing `parseRefreshTokenResponse` to throw in sync mode, or (b) at best does not reliably parse/persist the expiry field the comment/contract implies. This is a concrete correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The webhook handler has no error handling around `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)`, `symmetricDecrypt(...)`, or `JSON.parse(...)` — a malformed body, wrong encryption key, or invalid ciphertext throws an unhandled ZodError/crypto error and the route returns a 500. Any misconfigured or malformed sync push from the parent cal.com gets a 500 instead of a 4xx, and operators get no diagnostic signal distinguishing a bad key from a bad payload; retries from the parent will keep failing identically.

[ADVISORY] The diff introduces three non-trivial new behaviors — the credential-injection webhook endpoint (header auth, AES decryption, credential upsert), refreshOAuthTokens' sync-mode dispatch, and parseRefreshTokenResponse's dual-schema normalization — and contains zero test files (scanned the diff for spec/**, test/**, *.spec.*, *.test.*: none present), so none of the sync-mode paths that this review shows crashing or corrupting credentials are caught by CI. The exact failure modes above (Response-object misuse, placeholder refresh_token persistence, wrong userId for zoho-bigin) ship to production unverified; any regression in the webhook's auth or decryption also lands silently since no assertion covers this route.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce new sync-mode paths that are internally inconsistent and can crash/corrupt data. `refreshOAuthTokens()` returns a `fetch()` Response in sync mode, but several callers treat the return as a token object (e.g. GoogleCalendarService: `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;` where `fetch` Response has no `.data`). `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` returns a Zod `safeParse` result, but at least one caller stores it directly as the credential `key` (GoogleCalendarService: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...); ... data: { key }`), which would persist `{success,data/error}` instead of credentials. Additionally, Zoho Bigin calls `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`, passing what appears to be a credential id rather than `credential.userId`, which would send the wrong `calcomUserId` in sync mode. The finding’s point about lack of tests is supported by the diff (no test files added), but the more critical part—shipping these failure modes unverified—is grounded in the code changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The webhook endpoint gates only on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED (i.e. CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET + CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY) while every consumer of the sync feature (refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse) additionally requires CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, leaving the two gates of the same feature out of sync. A self-hosted operator who sets the webhook secret and encryption key but no sync endpoint gets a live, writable credential-injection webhook while their own instance never participates in token refresh — credentials injected by the parent will sit and rot as tokens expire with no local refresh path, and the half-enabled state is invisible in .env.example's setup instructions.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a configuration-gating mismatch: the new writable webhook `/api/webhook/app-credential` is enabled whenever `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is truthy (defined as `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in `packages/lib/constants.ts`), and does not require `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (see `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`). By contrast, the new sync-related helpers `refreshOAuthTokens` and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` only switch into “sync/parent-driven” behavior when both `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set. This can lead to an unintuitive partially-enabled configuration that isn’t clearly called out in `.env.example`. However, the finding’s claim that the instance then “never participates in token refresh” / has “no local refresh path” is not verifiable from the diff because `refreshOAuthTokens` explicitly falls back to the normal local refresh function when the sync endpoint is absent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The newly added Salesforce refresh block runs unconditionally inside connection setup — every time a jsforce.Connection is constructed the code fetches a fresh token from login.salesforce.com and writes it via prisma.credential.update, regardless of whether the existing access_token is expired. On any deployment with salesforce installed, each calendar operation that builds a service adds one outbound token request plus one credential DB write to the hot path, multiplying Salesforce API consumption and credential-row churn; token endpoint rate limits now gate ordinary calendar reads.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new token-refresh + DB update block added in `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` immediately after `const credentialKey = credential.key ...` and before `return new jsforce.Connection(...)`. It always `fetch`es `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then `await prisma.credential.update(...)` with the refreshed token, with no check for whether the existing `access_token` is expired. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/rate-limit concern (extra outbound call + credential write on every service/connection creation), though not necessarily a functional correctness failure by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sync mode the fetch Response returned by refreshOAuthTokens is passed directly to handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>, which expects Lark's envelope ({ code, data: { access_token, expire_time, ... } }), while the sync endpoint's documented response is a bare minimal token payload. With credential sync enabled, Lark token refresh cannot extract an access token from the sync response (the Lark envelope fields are absent), so Lark calendar operations fail on every refresh — lark is wired into the sync dispatch but not adapted to the minimal response shape it will receive.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the Lark refresh flow now calls `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then passes its return value (`resp`) into `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, this.log)`. But `refreshOAuthTokens` conditionally bypasses the Lark refresh URL and instead calls `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` and returns that raw `Response` when sync is enabled. The sync helper is explicitly commented as returning only a minimal token payload, not Lark’s native refresh endpoint response. There is no adaptation/parsing for the sync response shape in the Lark path (unlike other integrations that introduced `parseRefreshTokenResponse`), so with sync enabled this is likely to break token extraction/refresh for Lark.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response in sync mode while callers destructure app-specific shapes ({res}, .data, HubspotToken fields), so the credential-sync happy path throws or reads undefined for Google, Hubspot, Zoho and Zoho-Bigin. With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set (the feature's advertised deployment), googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts executes `const token = res?.data` on a fetch Response, gets undefined, then throws a TypeError on `token.access_token`; hubspot, zohocrm (`zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`) and zoho-bigin (`tokenInfo.data.error`) likewise dereference .data/fields that a Response does not have, so every token refresh in sharing mode crashes the calendar call instead of syncing credentials. The sync endpoint response contract was never adapted per app — the feature's core path was not traced through its own call sites.
matched_golden_ids: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. Both describe the same core bug: in credential-sync mode the refresh helper returns a raw fetch Response, but callers (e.g., GoogleCalendarService expecting res.data and Hubspot expecting a token object) assume an integration-specific token shape, leading to undefined/dereference runtime errors unless return type or call sites are updated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema uses `z.string().toString()` as computed keys, which evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" for both entries (the second overwrites the first), so the schema enforces nothing and zod's default strip mode drops access_token and expiry fields from the parsed data. In sync mode, parseRefreshTokenResponse returns data with access_token/expiry stripped: Google persists a credential key missing access_token and expiry_date via prisma.credential.update, so subsequent Google Calendar API calls fail authentication; the Salesforce caller spreads accessTokenParsed.data and loses instance_url, breaking the jsforce connection. The comment's stated invariant ("any property with a number is the expiry") is not enforced by any schema logic — the validation is a no-op that also corrupts stored credentials.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` defines computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]`, which evaluates to the literal key `"[object Object]"` (and the second such entry overwrites the first). This means the intended “any numeric property is expiry” validation is not actually enforced, and—because `z.object()` strips unknown keys by default—any fields not explicitly declared (e.g. `expiry_date`, `instance_url`, etc.) will be dropped from `refreshTokenResponse.data` in sync mode. The diff shows callers then consuming `.data` (e.g. Office365 merges it; Salesforce persists it), which can lead to persisted credentials missing required fields in subsequent runs. (The finding’s claim that `access_token` is stripped is not correct because `access_token` is explicitly declared, but the schema/key-loss problem itself is real and introduced here.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new Salesforce refresh block never routes through refreshOAuthTokens, so when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set it still refreshes against login.salesforce.com using this instance's own client_id/client_secret. For the stated audience (self-hosters whose parent application holds the real Salesforce app credentials), the local instance's client_secret does not match the parent's OAuth app, so the refresh call fails with invalid_client and Salesforce calendar sync is broken in exactly the deployments the feature targets — the sync feature is inconsistently scoped across the apps it touches in this diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new refresh logic directly `fetch`es `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` using local `consumer_key`/`consumer_secret` and never calls the newly introduced `refreshOAuthTokens` helper (unlike other integrations in this diff which were wrapped with `refreshOAuthTokens` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set). This makes Salesforce token refresh ignore the credential-sync pathway that the diff adds for self-hosted setups, creating inconsistent behavior across apps and potentially breaking refresh in the deployments the feature targets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse overwrites a missing refresh_token with the literal string "refresh_token" unconditionally — including in non-sync mode where the real provider refresh flow is used — and the fabricated value is then persisted to prisma.credential. A deployment that later disables credential sharing is left with credentials whose stored refresh_token is the placeholder "refresh_token"; the next real provider refresh sends that placeholder and the provider rejects it, permanently breaking that integration's token renewal with corrupted data written by the app itself.
matched_golden_ids: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: when the OAuth refresh response lacks a refresh_token, parseRefreshTokenResponse sets it to the literal string "refresh_token", persists it, and subsequent refresh attempts use the invalid placeholder causing authentication/refresh failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The redirectUri is changed from the appConfig.slug interpolation to a hardcoded `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback`, a drive-by change unrelated to credential sync. Behavior is unchanged only while appConfig.slug happens to be "zoho-bigin"; the slug now has two sources of truth (config.json for the callback handler, hardcoded string here), and the appConfig import in this file becomes dead for the URL — the next slug or rename change silently desyncs the add/callback pair. Not traceable to any requirement in this PR.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts`, `redirectUri` was changed from `WEBAPP_URL + `/api/integrations/${appConfig.slug}/callback`` to the hardcoded `WEBAPP_URL + `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback``. This creates a second source of truth for the slug (hardcoded here vs `appConfig.slug` used elsewhere, e.g. the callback file still imports `appConfig`), and can silently desync if the slug/config changes later. The diff alone doesn’t prove it breaks today (depends on what `appConfig.slug` is), so it’s a real review concern but not a verifiable defect from the diff by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new refresh fetch runs unconditionally before every jsforce connection creation (not gated on token expiry), and its success check `response.statusText !== "OK"` breaks under HTTP/2 where statusText is an empty string. Every Salesforce calendar operation now pays an extra token-refresh HTTP round trip plus a prisma.credential.update even when the stored token is still valid (hot-path regression on a path previously served with zero extra calls), and on any HTTP/2 response the statusText check throws HttpError 400 even for a successful refresh, disabling Salesforce sync entirely on such connections.

[ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is exported as the result of `&&` on two env strings (type string | undefined, not boolean), unlike every other boolean flag pattern in this constants file. Every consumer (webhook handler, parseRefreshTokenResponse, refreshOAuthTokens) must remember it is a truthy string rather than a boolean; the next consumer that does a strict `=== true` check or type-narrows it silently mis-gates the feature, and the exported surface documents the wrong contract for the flag.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/constants.ts`, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, which evaluates to a string (the second env value) or `undefined`, not a boolean. The current consumers in the diff use it in truthiness checks (e.g., `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` and `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && ...)`), so no immediate runtime defect is shown, but the exported name/contract implies a boolean and could lead to mis-gating if a consumer later does a strict boolean check or relies on boolean typing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The entire credential-sync feature surface added in this diff (webhook handler, refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse, and the per-app refresh rewiring across 7 services) ships with zero tests. The findings above (Response-shape mismatch, stripped schema keys, placeholder refresh_token) are exactly the class of regression tests would have caught; any future change to the sync contract or to one of the seven rewired refreshAccessToken closures silently breaks calendar/video syncing for all users of that app, discovered only at booking time.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new credential-sync functionality (new webhook API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, new helpers `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` and `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, and rewires multiple app refresh flows to use them), but the PR adds no accompanying test changes/files in the diff. Given the new branching behavior controlled by env flags (e.g., `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` in `packages/lib/constants.ts` and the endpoint-based alternate refresh path in `refreshOAuthTokens`), a lack of regression/contract tests for these new codepaths is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern even if it’s not itself a directly verifiable runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper ({success, data}), and the Google refresh path persists that wrapper object directly as the credential key (`data: { key }`), replacing the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` which returned the bare credentials. After the first token refresh, credential.key in the DB is `{success:true, data:{access_token,...}}` instead of the credentials object; every later GoogleCalendarService read (`credential.key as GoogleCredentials`) sees undefined access_token/refresh_token at the top level, so Google Calendar auth breaks for that user until manual repair.

[BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but its callers destructure provider-specific shapes: Google does `res?.data` (googleauth result shape) and Hubspot/Zoho-Bigin treat the return value as a parsed token/axios response. With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED + CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, Google's `token.access_token` throws TypeError (Response has no `.data`), and Hubspot/Zoho-Bigin read undefined token fields and persist undefined/NaN expiry into credential rows — token refresh is broken and can destroy stored credentials for every sync-mode deployment.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `refreshOAuthTokens` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, does `const response = await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` and returns that raw `Response` object (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). Callers still assume provider-specific return shapes: GoogleCalendarService assigns `const token = res?.data` and then reads `token.access_token`/`token.expiry_date` (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts), which will fail because a fetch `Response` has no `.data`. Hubspot and Zoho-Bigin similarly treat the return as a parsed token/axios response (`HubspotToken` and `tokenInfo.data...`), but in sync mode they will receive a `Response` without those fields, breaking refresh and potentially leading to bad persistence paths when those undefined fields are used downstream.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The minimumTokenResponseSchema catch-all keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the string "[object Object]" (Object.prototype.toString on a Zod instance), so the schema is `{access_token, "[object Object]"}` and the intended 'any numeric property is the expiry' wildcard never matches; zod's default stripping then drops every field except access_token. In sync mode the parsed token response contains only access_token — expiry_date/expires_in and any other fields are silently stripped, so downstream expiry computations get undefined/NaN even once the Response-shape bug is fixed.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` defines computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions are evaluated immediately to a single string key (very likely `"[object Object]"`), not a wildcard/catch-all. The second computed key also overwrites the first, so the schema effectively becomes `{ access_token, "[object Object]"?: ... }` and, because `z.object()` strips unknown keys by default, real token fields like `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, etc. will be dropped in the `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` path. This matches the finding that sync-mode parsing can silently lose expiry-related fields.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Zoho-Bigin refresh call passes `credentialId` as the userId argument of refreshOAuthTokens, while every other call site (google-calendar, hubspot, zohocrm, lark, zoom, webex, o365) passes `credential.userId` — a confusable-pair binding where the credential row id is sent as calcomUserId. In sync mode the CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT receives the credential's database id in the `calcomUserId` field, so the parent application resolves the wrong user (or none) and returns/updates credentials for the wrong account, silently corrupting or failing Zoho-Bigin token sync.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credentialId` into the `userId` parameter (per `refreshOAuthTokens` signature: `(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId: number | null)`). All other updated call sites pass `credential.userId`. In sync mode, `refreshOAuthTokens` sends this value as `calcomUserId` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, so using a credential identifier variable instead of the user’s id would cause the sync endpoint to look up the wrong user or none.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Salesforce is the only app whose refresh path was not routed through refreshOAuthTokens — it performs a direct hardcoded fetch to login.salesforce.com unconditionally, creating a parallel refresh service path outside the credential-sync architecture introduced in this diff. In a credential-sharing deployment, Salesforce refreshes tokens directly against the provider (rotating the refresh token), so cal.com's stored copy diverges and is invalidated — the shared-credential invariant this PR establishes is broken for the salesforce app.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a credential-sharing/credential-sync refresh architecture via `refreshOAuthTokens` (used in Google, Hubspot, Lark, O365, Webex, Zoho, Zoom, etc.), which conditionally calls `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true. However, `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` adds a new refresh flow that unconditionally does a direct `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` using `credentialKey.refresh_token`, and does not route through `refreshOAuthTokens`. In a credential-sharing deployment, other integrations can avoid needing a real refresh token locally (e.g., `parseRefreshTokenResponse` injects a dummy `refresh_token` when sync is enabled), so Salesforce bypassing this path is inconsistent and can break the intended shared-credential invariant/behavior by attempting a provider refresh locally instead of using the sync endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The webhook uses findFirst-then-update/create (explicitly noted 'Can't use prisma upsert') with no unique constraint on Credential(userId, appId) backing the check, so concurrent webhook deliveries race the SELECT and both fall into the create branch. Two concurrent sync pushes for the same user+app create duplicate Credential rows; downstream code that picks the user's calendar/video credential gets an ambiguous, possibly stale duplicate, and every subsequent webhook updates only one of the rows while reads may select the other.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does a non-atomic `findFirst` followed by either `credential.update` or `credential.create`. With concurrent webhook deliveries for the same `{ userId, appId }`, both requests can observe no row and both execute `credential.create`, leading to duplicate credentials if no unique constraint exists, or a create failure if a unique constraint does exist (neither case is handled). This race is directly present in the diff and can break downstream reads that assume a single credential per user+app.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The newly added Salesforce token-refresh fetch and prisma.credential.update run unconditionally on every service construction, with no expiry check, on a hot path (every calendar operation instantiates the service). Every Salesforce calendar read/write now issues an external token HTTP call plus a DB write even when the stored token is still valid, adding latency and provider rate-limit pressure to the booking path for all Salesforce users.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff adds an unconditional refresh flow: it immediately `fetch`es `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` using the stored `refresh_token`, then `await prisma.credential.update({ ... })` before creating the `jsforce.Connection`. There is no expiry/validity check or conditional guard around this refresh+DB write, so every time this code path runs it will incur an external HTTP call and a DB update even if the existing `access_token` is still usable. This is a concrete diff-grounded latency/rate-limit concern, but not a clear correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The sync-mode fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout, no response.ok/status check, and no retry or fallback, and it sits synchronously inside token refresh on the booking path. A slow or erroring credential-sync endpoint hangs or degrades every calendar/video operation for all users (fetch has no default timeout), turning one dependent service into a global availability dependency with no graceful degradation.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the sync-mode branch does `await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` and immediately returns the `response` without any timeout/abort handling, without checking `response.ok`/status, and without any retry or fallback logic. This code is awaited inside multiple integrations’ token refresh paths (e.g., Google/Office365/Zoom/Webex services), so a slow or failing sync endpoint can directly slow down or fail those operations. The broader “global availability dependency for all users” framing is somewhat extrapolative, but the lack of timeout/status handling and synchronous dependency is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The decrypted `keys` payload is JSON.parse'd and persisted via credential.create/update with no per-app zod schema validation, unlike every other credential write path in the app-store which validates before persisting. A payload encrypted with a wrong/mismatched key decrypts to garbage or a wrong-shaped object that is stored verbatim as the user's credential key, silently bricking that user's app integration with no validation error to surface the cause.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the payload is decrypted and immediately `JSON.parse`d (`const keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))`) and then persisted verbatim via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: keys }})` / `create({ data: { key: keys, ... }})` with no app-specific schema validation. This allows wrong-shaped (but JSON-valid) decrypted data to be stored as the credential `key`, which can corrupt/bricked integrations. The diff shows no zod/parsing step for `keys` beyond JSON parsing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When the token response has no refresh_token, the code writes the literal sentinel string "refresh_token" into the parsed data, which callers then persist as the credential's real refresh_token. The sentinel is stored as data in the DB; if CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is later unset while APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED stays on (or vice versa), the next direct refresh sends the literal string "refresh_token" to the provider as a refresh token, permanently breaking that credential's refresh.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `parseRefreshTokenResponse` which, on a successful parse, forcibly sets `refresh_token` to the literal string "refresh_token" when the provider response lacks it (`if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }`). Call sites then use the parsed data to update persisted credentials (e.g., Office365: spreads `tokenResponse.data` into `o365AuthCredentials` and then updates Prisma; Zoom: assigns `parsedToken = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` in the refresh flow; similar pattern elsewhere). This means a missing refresh_token can overwrite the stored real refresh token with the sentinel. If later `refreshOAuthTokens` switches back to using the direct provider refresh (e.g., `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` removed while `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` remains truthy), the code will send the literal "refresh_token" as the refresh token, breaking the credential.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Credential matching is keyed on (userId, appId) only, but Credential rows created before appId existed (or by paths that set only `type`) have appId null, so the lookup misses them and the create branch inserts a second credential with the same `type` for the same user. Legacy installs accumulate duplicate credentials per app per user; consumers that pick the user's calendar credential by type now face multiple rows with no defined winner, so bookings may bind to the stale non-synced copy.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), the existing credential lookup is `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId: reqBody.userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })`. If a user already has a credential record for the same integration but with `appId` unset (e.g., `null`) or otherwise not equal to `appMetadata.slug`, this code will not find it and will go down the `create` branch, creating an additional credential row for the same user/integration. The diff does not show whether such legacy rows exist or how other consumers select credentials (by `type` vs `appId`), so the downstream impact described is not fully verifiable from the diff alone, but the missing fallback/migration path is a concrete edge case created/exposed by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The design establishes two concurrent writers for the same credential records — a push webhook (app-credential.ts) and a pull refresh endpoint (refreshOAuthTokens) — with no coordination, versioning, or single-source-of-truth rule for which copy wins. When parent and child both refresh (e.g. a scheduled refresh on cal.com racing a booking-triggered refresh on the child), each side persists its own newer token and last-writer-wins; for providers that rotate refresh tokens the losing side's stored refresh_token is invalidated, permanently breaking that user's integration.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new webhook writer that upserts `prisma.credential` records (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` does `credential.update/create` with `data: { key: keys }`) and also introduces new refresh flows that update the same credential records during token refresh (e.g. `GoogleCalendarService`, `Office365CalendarService`, `Zoom` adapters call `prisma.credential.update` with refreshed token material). There is no diff-visible coordination mechanism (no optimistic locking/version field, no "source of truth" guard, no conflict resolution), so concurrent updates can be last-writer-wins and clobber each other. The specific "parent vs child" race and "rotating refresh tokens permanently breaking" outcome depends on external deployment behavior not shown here, but the uncoordinated concurrent-writer design concern is grounded in the new code paths.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, the function returns the result of `fetch(...)`, i.e. a raw `Response` object.
